title: Studies in Islamic Mysticism
author: Reynold A. Nicholson
description: Studies in Islamic Mysticism by Reynold A. Nicholson (Cambridge University Press, 1921), the great Cambridge scholar of Sufism and translator of Rumi. In three substantial studies Nicholson examines key figures and ideas of Sufism. The first is a study of the life of Abu Sa'id ibn Abi'l-Khayr (967-1049), the Persian Sufi saint famed for his quatrains and ecstatic practice. The second, on 'the Perfect Man', analyses the doctrine of al-Insan al-Kamil in the work of Abd al-Karim al-Jili, developing Ibn Arabi's teaching on the human being as the microcosm and the mirror of divine names. The third is a study of the Odes (Ta'iyya and others) of the Arab mystical poet Ibn al-Farid, with translations and commentary. Combining translation and analysis, it remains a classic of Western Sufi scholarship.
